scope: Screen BRL-CAD's DXF converters as an optional independent consumer for explicit faceted geometry, reconcile current and legacy published converter scope, and record safety and claim boundaries.

method.kind: Primary-source project documentation and issue/PR status review reconciled with existing plan owners
localInspection: DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md: existing BRL-CAD POLYFACE issue and PAR-37/7V boundaries
DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md: existing explicit-geometry and composed-consumer checkpoints
method.evidenceBoundary: Documentation establishes only a candidate converter route and declared semantics. Current and legacy DXF entity scope is not reconciled by a pinned executable. Issue #228 is a BRL-CAD peer report, not a libdxfrw defect or a security audit of any local code. No peer runtime or native qualification occurred.

evidence.topic: BRL-CAD provides a potentially useful explicit-facet consumer route
observed: The current conversion tutorial describes polygons and meshes importing as BOT primitives and each DXF layer as a region.
The import route documents missing DXF units defaulting to millimeters and provides scale and tolerance options; the documented default tolerance is 0.005 mm.
The export route documents 3DFACE as the default and a -p option for POLYFACE MESH output.
doesNotEstablish: exact entity coverage for a current pinned BRL-CAD build
preservation of per-entity handles, blocks, attributes, or owner graphs
ACIS/SAT/SAB parsing, DWG/AcDs reading, analytic curved surfaces, or B-rep identity
evidence.planUse: Keep as an optional composed-checkpoint candidate for generated explicit 3D facet/mesh controls only. Pin the tool build and options, and compare measured facets, bounds, orientation/closure, and analytic volume with an independently authored manifest.

evidence.topic: Published DXF importer scope is inconsistent across documentation generations
observed: The older conversion guide says dxf-g predates ACIS in DXF, does not support ACIS, and converts only 3DFACES and 3DMESH.
The current tutorial describes polygon and mesh conversion more broadly but does not provide the same exact entity-by-entity matrix.
evidence.planUse: Before scoring any family, run a single pinned-build smoke check on locally generated 3DFACE, 3DMESH, and POLYLINE/PFACE inputs separately; keep undocumented or rejected families out of the result denominator.

evidence.topic: BRL-CAD dxf-g is not admitted as a hostile-input safety oracle
observed: The current issue index lists issue #228, a report of out-of-bounds access in dxf-g from attacker-controlled POLYLINE face indices.

A proposed guard in PR #245 was previously inspected; its lower-bound rule is not a replacement for the signed face-index semantics in the authoritative DXF contract and existing local PAR-37/7V controls.
Issue or PR presence does not establish a release fix or a matching defect in libdxfrw.
evidence.planUse: Never feed hostile/adversarial drawings to this candidate or count it as a secure-parser pass. If used, use only small valid locally generated controls with in-range positive face references, keep the run optional, and retain local negative/sentinel polyface coverage.

nextActions: Continue the current local implementation queue; do not wait for BRL-CAD availability or run it on every slice.
At the existing composed explicit-geometry checkpoint only, consider one pinned BRL-CAD smoke run if an appropriate build is already available.
Generate valid controls from scratch in a disposable location; pin input hashes, tool version, command, units, scale, tolerance, warnings, output mapping, and measured geometry.
Keep any result limited to the observed explicit faceted geometry route; it does not qualify entity/owner preservation, DWG, ACIS/AcDs, B-rep semantics, or native downstream applications.
Keep J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 DEFERRED_EXTERNAL and non-promoting.
